label: rem:q-gl-fiber-functor-sketch
title: Proof sketch for fibre-functor mediation
html:
The equivalence is pinned by the Tannakian rigidity of the fibre functor \tau: once \tau is fixed, reconstructing the dual group, transporting the Hecke datum, and closing uniqueness admit no freedom. The proof realises this in three steps.

Concretely, the archetype to keep in mind is a rank-one q-local system \mathcal{L}_q together with the single q-Hecke eigensheaf it governs; the general statement replaces this pair by the full tensor categories on either side.

Step 1: Tannakian reconstruction of \check{G}_q. By fibre-functor rigidity, the fibre functor \tau \colon \mathbf{Rep}(G_q) \to \mathrm{Vect} is unique up to unique isomorphism. Tannaka--Krein reconstruction gives G_q \cong \mathrm{Aut}^\otimes(\tau). Applying root-system duality and inversion q \mapsto q^{-1} yields \check{G}_q and its canonical fibre functor \check{\tau}.

Step 2: Hecke data determines \mathbb{L}_q. Let \mathcal{M} be a q-Hecke eigensheaf with eigenvalue \mathcal{L}_q. The collection of isomorphisms \{\mathbf{T}_{x,\lambda}^{(q)}(\mathcal{M}) \simeq \mathcal{M} \otimes V_\lambda^{(q)}(\mathcal{L}_q)_x\} defines a tensor functor \mathbf{Rep}(\check{G}_q) \to \mathrm{Vect}_X. This functor is a point of \mathrm{LocSys}_{\check{G}_q}(X) (q-Hecke eigenvalue determination). Conversely, the Hecke correspondence sends every q-local system \mathcal{L}_q to a q-\mathcal{D}-module \mathbb{L}_q^{-1}(\mathcal{L}_q) on \mathrm{Bun}_{G_q}.

Step 3: Uniqueness from rigidity. Suppose \mathbb{L}_q and \mathbb{L}_q' both satisfy properties (1)--(3) of the q-Geometric Langlands conjecture. The composition \mathbb{L}_q' \circ \mathbb{L}_q^{-1} is a tensor auto-equivalence of \mathrm{QCoh}(\mathrm{LocSys}_{\check{G}_q}(X)) that preserves the tautological q-local system. By the rigidity of \tau, this auto-equivalence is uniquely isomorphic to the identity. \square
